segments.he: עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת בְּטוּחִים מִכָּל צַר וְאוֹיֵב וּמַסְטִין
segments.en: And these four encampments are the aspect of the four camps of the Shechinah, drawn from the dalet of "Hear O Israel, Hashem is our G-d, Hashem is One" — where the essential self-nullification to the Will of the Infinite lies. And all this is the aspect of prayer, conversation, and hisbodidus — for the essential conversation and hisbodidus must reach the point where one nullifies oneself, nullifying all one's will to the Will of G-d. And this is the aspect of mishpat [judgment, self-reckoning] that is mentioned in Rabbainu's words in many places — that a person must judge himself regarding every matter, whether it is fitting to spend his days thus. And it is explained in the Torah "Heichal HaKodesh" [Likutay Moharan I:59] that this aspect of mishpat is the aspect of a ravua [square — fourfold], the aspect of the Breastplate of Judgment, of which it is said "it shall be square, folded double."

segments.he: וְזֶהוּ הֵן עַם לְבָדָד יִשְׁכּן. שֶׁהֵם עַם קָדוֹשׁ כָּזֶה שֶׁשּׁוֹכְנִים לְבָדָד. שֶׁהֵם מְקַיְּמִים לֵךְ עַמִּי בּא בַּחֲדָרֶיךָ וּסְגוֹר דְּלָתֶיךָ בַּעֲדֶךָ חֲבִי כִּמְעַט רֶגַע עַד יַעֲבר זָעַם (יְשַׁעְיָה כ"ו): שֶׁהֵם מִתְבּוֹדְדִים בֵּינָם לְבֵין קוֹנָם וְשׁוֹפְכִים שִׂיחָתָם לְפָנָיו בְּכָל פַּעַם וְחוֹשְׁבִים בְּכָל יוֹם עַל אַחֲרִיתָם וְסוֹפָם הָאַחֲרוֹן. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם בְּטוּחִים מִכָּל צַר וְאוֹיֵב וּמַסְטִין כִּי הֵם מַסְתִּירִים עַצְמָם בְּצֵל כְּנָפָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד בִּבְחִינַת (תְּהִלִּים ל"ב) אַתָּה סֵתֶר לִי וְכוּ' שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת וַיִּשְׁכּן יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּטַח בָּדָד עֵין יַעֲקב וְכוּ' (דְּבָרִים ל"ג) בְּחִינַת כִּי אַתָּה ה' לְבָדָד לָבֶטַח תּוֹשִׁיבֵנִי (תְּהִלִּים ד'):
segments.en: For the essential hisbodidus and conversation must be in the strengthening of good will toward G-d, until one is included in His oneness in the aspect of the dalet of Echad — from whatever direction one may be, in the aspect of "Come from the four winds, O breath" [Yechezkel 37:9] — that from all four directions of the world, to which one's mind has scattered, one should return from all of them to the dalet of Echad, to be included in the spirit of G-d, which is His Will. For ruach [spirit/wind] also means ratzon [will]. For this is the essence of hisbodidus — that one must seclude oneself and contemplate where one is in the world, and to where one's mind and thought and will has scattered, and to where one has been thrown and led astray through one's deeds and thoughts. Until one generally sees that one has no place or direction from any of the four directions of the world to flee to, to hide from the troubles of the world — physical and spiritual, in body and soul and money and livelihood — in the manner of "Where shall I go from Your spirit?" [Tehillim 139:7], and: "I will lift my eyes to the mountains — from where will my help come?" [ibid. 121:1], and: "I look to the right and see — no one recognizes me; every escape has been lost to me" [ibid. 142:5]. Until one sees that there is no escape except to Him alone — in the aspect of "from You I have fled, and to You I return". And therefore this aspect of mishpat — which is the aspect of hisbodidus — is called ravua [fourfold, square], in the aspect of "the number of a quarter of Israel." For whoever engages in this truthfully turns in his words toward every side of the four directions, until he sees his distress and his toil and his bitterness, that he has no place to flee but to G-d, to be included in the dalet of Echad.

segments.he: שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת בָּדָד בְּחִינַת הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת עַל עַל יְדֵי זֶה שׁוֹכֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּטַח תָּמִיד. כִּי מִי זֶה עָרֵב אֶת לִבּוֹ לָגֶשֶׁת אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֵם מַסְתִּירִים עַצְמָן אֶצְלוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְחִינַת (שָׁם צ"א) לא תִירָא מִפַּחַד לַיְלָה מֵחֵץ יָעוּף יוֹמָם וְכוּ' וְכוּ' רַק בְּעֵינֶיךָ תַּבִּיט שָׂמִים מְעוֹנָם וְדִירָתָם וּמִבְטָחָם אֶצְלוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי הִתְבּוֹדְדוּתָם שֶׁעוֹסְקִים לְסַלֵּק מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם מִכָּל הַהֲבָלִים שֶׁל זֶה הָעוֹלָם וּלְבַטֵּל רְצוֹנָם אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְזֶהוּ (בְּמִדְבַּר כ"ג) וּבַגּוֹיִם לא יִתְחַשָּׁב וְתַרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן וִירוּשַׁלְמִי וּבְנִמּוּס עֲמָמַיָּא לָא מִתְעַרְבִין שֶׁאֵינָם רוֹדְפִין אַחַר נִמּוּסֵי הָעַכּוּ"ם וְאַחַר רִבּוּי כְּלֵי בַּיִת וּכְלֵי כֶּסֶף וְתַכְשִׁיטִין וְכוּ' וּשְׁאָרֵי דְּבָרִים הַמַּרְבִּים הֶבֶל שֶׁלָּהֶם. רַק מְסַלְּקִים כָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם מִכָּל זֶה וּמִתְבּוֹדְדִים וְשׁוֹפְכִים שִׂיחָם בִּרְצוֹנוֹת טוֹבִים וְכִסּוּפִין חֲזָקִים וְגַעְגּוּעִים נִמְרָצִים אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
segments.en: For G-d is found at all times for all who call upon Him, even if they have strayed as far as they have strayed — for His compassion is never exhausted. And this is: "And the number of a quarter of Israel" — that no one can count and tell what comes from the aspect of the "quarter of Israel" — which is judgment and hisbodidus — how they return from all the places to which they have strayed, to G-d, to be included in His oneness in the dalet of Echad, through genuine strengthening of will. For it is certainly impossible to estimate what is accomplished through this.

And whoever merits to strengthen himself in this — to have his will strong always toward the truth, and to never relax the good will even when various things befall him — certainly ultimately his end will be good. For about this it was said: "May my soul die the death of the upright, and may my end be like his" [Bamidbar 23:10]. For Bilaam said of himself that he knew his own terrible corruption and pollution, the like of which has no comparison — yet even so, he said: "Would that even I could merit to go in this path — to strengthen myself from now onward with good desires and to pour out my speech each day before Him and to judge myself at all times in the above manner — then I too would merit a good end, in the manner of 'and may my end be like his.'"
